title: Loop back: nested decisions
idea: LOOP. No new concept. Review a choice inside a choice - trace the outer gate then the inner decision.

exercises.explanation: member is True (outer passes), then age 70 >= 65 (inner passes): 'Senior member discount'. (Review of nested if.)

exercises.prompt: Same code, but member = False. What prints?
exercises.explanation: The outer gate fails, so the inner decision is skipped and the outer else runs. (Review of outer gate.)

exercises.prompt: An inner if only runs when the outer condition is true.
exercises.explanation: The inner block is trapped inside the outer branch, so it needs the outer to pass first. (Review of nesting.)

exercises.prompt: To debug a nested decision, you should trace...
options: the outer condition first, then the inner one
exercises.explanation: Outer decides whether inner runs, so check it first. (Review of tracing nesting.)
8 > 0 (outer), and 8 % 2 == 0 (inner), so 'Positive even'. (Review of nested if with %.)

exercises.prompt: For the code above, what does n = 7 give?
exercises.explanation: 7 > 0 (outer passes), 7 % 2 is 1 (inner else), so 'Positive odd'. (Review of inner else.)

exercises.prompt: For the same code, what does n = -4 give?
exercises.explanation: -4 is not > 0, so the outer else runs and the inner even/odd check is skipped. (Review of outer gate.)

exercises.prompt: If a nested inner check should apply to everyone, it should NOT be trapped inside a stricter outer condition.
exercises.explanation: Nesting creates a dependency. If the inner rule is universal, the nesting is a bug. (Review of nesting choices.)

exercises.prompt: Order the steps to trace a nested decision for one input.
blocks: If it passes, check the inner condition
exercises.explanation: Outer, then inner, then the branch. Trace nesting from outside in. (Review of tracing.)

exercises.prompt: A discount applies only to members. Non-members never get it. Is the members-only nesting a bug?
options: No - if the rule is members-only, the nesting is correct
exercises.explanation: Whether nesting is a bug depends on the intended rule. Members-only nesting matches a members-only rule. (Review of reasoning about structure.)
